items.title_en: Financial Expert: Don't Abandon This Volatile Market
paras: 通膨、利率與伊朗戰事交織，美股連企業繳出亮眼財報都未必買單。美國財經名嘴、CNBC 節目主持人 Jim Cramer 週三 (14 日) 表示，市場走向雖然難以預測，投資人此時若全面退出股市，可能來不及在下一波漲勢啟動前重新進場，反而錯失關鍵報酬。
美股週三收黑，標普 500 指數下跌逾 1%，那斯達克綜合指數下挫 1.9%，道瓊工業指數則小幅收低。
Cramer指出，當經濟數據與企業財報都無法提供明確方向，投資人確實很難維持信心，但這不代表出清持股就是較好的選擇。
他形容，這樣的行情讓人只想把股票全賣掉、回家休息。然而，一旦離場，投資人能否及時買回，趕上一年中貢獻主要漲幅的少數交易日，他對此抱持懷疑。
摩根大通的研究也凸顯錯過上漲日的代價。
假設投資人在 2005 年至 2024 年間，將 1 萬美元投入標普 500 指數，若錯過期間表現最好的 10 個交易日，期末資產將不到全程持有者的一半。
Cramer以週三公布的美國通膨數據說明，市場反應有多難掌握。
美國 9 月消費者物價指數 (CPI) 月增 0.6%，略高於預期，帶動美債殖利率一度走高，隨後卻轉而下滑，即使油價仍持續上漲。
一般而言，通膨高於預期，會強化市場對聯準會 (Fed) 加大升息力道的預期，進而推升殖利率。但這次債市走勢反覆，讓投資人更難判斷下一步政策及其影響。
在Cramer看來，Fed 正面臨兩難：再度升息可能拖慢經濟，維持利率不變則可能讓長期借貸成本進一步攀升。
不過，若伊朗戰爭結束，油價可能大幅回落，讓通膨在 Fed 無須進一步採取行動的情況下獲得緩解。
企業財報同樣未能替市場指引方向。
摩根士丹利 (MS-US) 當季業績表現不差，股價仍下跌近 3%；半導體設備大廠艾司摩爾 (ASML-US) 公布強勁財報、需求持續成長，股價卻由早盤上漲轉為收跌約 4%，隨晶片股一同承壓。
Cramer表示，這種基本面與股價反應難以對應的市場，確實讓人難以堅定持股信心，但即使退場能避開後續跌勢，投資人仍須面對另一項風險：市場恢復上漲時，自己可能已不在場內。
paras_en: Inflation, interest rates and the Iran war are intertwining, and even stellar corporate earnings on Wall Street may not be enough to win over investors. CNBC host and U.S. financial commentator Jim Cramer said on Wednesday (the 14th) that although market direction is hard to predict, if investors completely exit the stock market now they may miss the chance to re‑enter before the next rally starts, thereby losing key returns.
U.S. stocks closed lower on Wednesday, with the S&P 500 down more than 1%, the Nasdaq Composite falling 1.9%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipping only slightly.

Cramer noted that when economic data and corporate earnings provide no clear direction, investors understandably find it hard to stay confident, but that does not mean liquidating positions is the better choice.

He described the market as making you want to sell all your stocks and go home to rest. Yet once you’re out, he doubts investors can get back in time to catch the few trading days that contributed most of the year’s gains.
JPMorgan research also highlights the cost of missing up‑days.

Assuming an investor had put $10,000 into the S&P 500 between 2005 and 2024, missing the ten best trading days in that period would leave the ending balance at less than half of what a fully‑invested holder would have earned.
Cramer used Wednesday’s U.S. inflation data to illustrate how hard market reactions can be to gauge.
U.S. September consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.6% month‑over‑month, slightly above expectations, pushing Treasury yields up briefly before they fell again, even as oil prices kept climbing.

Generally, higher‑than‑expected inflation strengthens expectations that the Fed will hike rates further, which lifts yields. This time, however, the bond market’s back‑and‑forth made it even harder for investors to judge the next policy move and its impact.
In Cramer’s view, the Fed faces a dilemma: raising rates again could slow the economy, while keeping rates steady could let long‑term borrowing costs climb further.
But if the Iran war ends, oil prices could drop sharply, easing inflation enough that the Fed might not need to take additional action.
Corporate earnings also failed to give the market a clear guide.

Morgan Stanley (MS-US) posted decent quarterly results yet its stock fell nearly 3%; semiconductor equipment giant ASML (ASML-US) reported strong earnings and growing demand, but its share price swung from an early‑session rise to a roughly 4% decline, pressured along with other chip stocks.

Cramer said that a market where fundamentals and price reactions are so mismatched makes it hard to stay confident in holdings, but even if exiting avoids further drops, investors still face another risk: when the market rebounds, they may no longer be in the game.

items.title: 澤倫斯基再向歐盟求援！2027年再求700億歐元 歐洲籌資陷兩難
items.title_en: Zelensky Again Appeals to EU for Aid! Seeks Additional €70 Billion for 2027, Europe Faces Funding Dilemma
paras: 烏克蘭總統澤倫斯基（Volodymyr Zelenskyy）週五(16日)在歐盟總部，對著一眾歐洲領導人提出一系列援助請求。
綜合央視新聞等媒體報導和澤倫斯基演講稿，其主要訴求包括：為2027年爭取至少額外700億歐元資金支持，緊急獲得300枚「愛國者」防空系統攔截彈以應對冬季襲擊，同時推動歐盟確保被凍結的俄羅斯資產能夠實際用於支持烏克蘭。
澤倫斯基談到：「明年，這場戰爭將耗費1550億歐元。我們還需要至少700億歐元的額外資金，用於國防、武器以及增強我們的韌性。這是一個現實的數字。」
烏克蘭總統舉例稱，無人機在這場戰爭中發揮著重要作用，烏克蘭目前有能力將無人機產量提高至現有水平的兩至三倍，但缺乏足夠資金來實現這一目標。
據媒體報導，儘管歐洲國家多數站在支持烏克蘭的立場上，但澤倫斯基提出的新要求令不少國家感到為難。歐盟峰會當天未就新增資金作出具體決定，相關融資方案仍有待進一步評估。
歐盟此前已同意向烏克蘭提供900億歐元貸款。2025年12月，歐盟領導人就這一安排達成協議；今年4月23日，歐盟理事會完成最後一項關鍵立法程序，為資金發放掃清法律障礙。
按照歐盟公布的安排，這筆貸款中，600億歐元用於支持烏克蘭國防工業和採購軍事裝備，另外300億歐元用於宏觀金融援助及政府預算支持。資金通過歐盟在資本市場舉債籌集，以歐盟預算作為擔保，計畫覆蓋烏克蘭2026年至2027年的資金需求。
根據歐盟的資金安排，2026年計畫提供450億歐元，餘下450億歐元留待2027年。
因此，一些成員國對澤倫斯基的新要求提出疑問。奧地利總理Christian Stocker週五表示，歐盟此前已經為烏克蘭2026年至2027年提供超過900億歐元資金。根據他掌握的資訊，目前僅使用約200億歐元，理論上仍有相當大的資金空間。
Stocker直言，烏克蘭必須透明地解釋新增財政缺口的來源，他也對這一數字感到驚訝。
斯洛伐克總理Robert Fico也在當天歐盟峰會後表示，澤倫斯基要求歐盟為2027年再提供700億歐元貸款，但他已經在談判中明確強調：斯洛伐克不會參與這筆新增貸款。
Fico認為，烏克蘭最終可能無力償還這些貸款，因此所謂的貸款實際上可能等同於贈款。
捷克同樣對擴大歐盟援烏融資持審慎態度。總理Andrej Babiš反對將歐盟下一輪多年期預算中擬議的約1000億歐元烏克蘭貸款安排納入預算，並強調捷克不會為相關借款提供擔保。
一名歐洲外交人士此前透露，國際貨幣基金組織預計將在11月公布新的評估報告，屆時歐盟才能更準確地判斷烏克蘭的資金需求，並討論是否再次共同舉債、動用現有預算資源或要求成員國分別出資。
即使支持援烏的國家，也承認700億歐元存在籌資難題。愛沙尼亞總理Kristen Michal表示，歐盟可能需要再次向烏克蘭提供貸款，彌補2027年的財政缺口。
他認為，資金援助對烏克蘭維持戰爭能力至關重要，但目前最有可能的解決方案是歐盟再次共同舉債。他希望歐洲各國能在2026年底前敲定2027年的額外援助，以避免受到明年歐洲多國選舉的影響。
在這方面，法國2027年總統大選熱門候選人、極右翼領導人勒龐（Marine Le Pen）本週早些時候對媒體表示，法國已無力承擔更多援烏費用。
勒龐表示：「公平的做法是告訴澤倫斯基，實際上也是警告他：我們不能再提供更多援助了。」
她還表示，如果自己在2027年成為法國總統，可能不會支持繼續通過歐盟機制擴大對烏克蘭的貸款。
至於動用凍結俄羅斯資產一事，比利時首相Bart De Wever週四強調，被凍結的資產應當在戰爭結束後的和平協議中處理，而不是現在就加以使用。歐盟境內被凍結的俄羅斯資產超過2000億歐元，其中絕大部分由比利時境內的歐洲清算銀行持有。
相比2027年的資金需求，烏克蘭對防空導彈的需求顯得更加迫切。
據週四相關報導，一名了解情況的消息人士透露，烏克蘭已經耗盡美製「愛國者」防空系統的攔截彈，使其在面對俄羅斯彈道導彈襲擊時更加脆弱。
這名消息人士表示，在最近一輪襲擊中，由於缺乏攔截彈，俄軍發射的彈道導彈幾乎全部未被攔截。
但要從歐洲國家獲得更多攔截彈，同樣並不容易。歐洲各國自身庫存並不寬裕，而全球彈藥供應緊張，也使補充庫存面臨壓力。與此同時，烏克蘭與美國的關係持續緊張，歐洲國家未來能否順利從美國獲得補充導彈，也存在不確定性。
據媒體援引歐洲外交人士說法，西班牙政府擔心，由於美國總統川普與西班牙首相桑切斯（Pedro Sánchez）關係緊張，未來可能無法從美國獲得足夠的補充導彈，因此對於進一步削減現有庫存持謹慎態度。
希臘的顧慮則主要來自自身安全環境。雅典長期擔憂與鄰國土耳其之間的緊張關係，擔心削減防空儲備可能被視為自身防禦能力下降的信號。
另據報導，川普政府近日曾警告烏克蘭和歐洲盟友，如果基輔不停止對俄羅斯能源設施的縱深打擊，美國可能暫停通過歐洲國家採購美國武器援烏的安排。
paras_en: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Friday (the 16th) addressed a crowd of European leaders at the EU headquarters with a series of aid requests.

According to reports from CCTV News and other media and Zelenskyy's speech text, his main demands are: to secure at least an extra €70 billion for 2027, to obtain urgently 300 Patriot air‑defence interceptors to cope with winter attacks, and to push the EU to ensure that frozen Russian assets can actually be used to support Ukraine.
Zelensky said: "Next year this war will cost €155 billion. We still need at least €70 billion in additional funding for defence, weapons and to boost our resilience. That is a realistic figure."

The Ukrainian president gave an example that drones play a crucial role in the war; Ukraine now has the capacity to raise drone production to two‑ to three‑times its current level but lacks sufficient funds to achieve that goal.

Media reports say that although most European countries stand behind Ukraine, Zelensky's new demands put many states in a difficult position. The EU summit that day did not make a concrete decision on the additional money, and the financing plan remains to be further evaluated.

The EU had previously agreed to provide Ukraine with a €90 billion loan. In December 2025 EU leaders reached an agreement on that arrangement; on 23 April this year the EU Council completed the final key legislative step, clearing legal obstacles to disbursement.

Under the EU’s announced scheme, €60 billion of the loan is earmarked for Ukraine’s defence industry and military procurement, and another €30 billion for macro‑financial assistance and government budget support. The funds will be raised by EU borrowing in capital markets, guaranteed by the EU budget, and are intended to cover Ukraine’s needs for 2026‑2027.
According to the EU’s schedule, €45 billion is planned for 2026, with the remaining €45 billion reserved for 2027.

Consequently, some member states have questioned Zelensky’s new request. Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said on Friday that the EU has already pledged over €90 billion for Ukraine for 2026‑2027. Based on the information he has, only about €20 billion has been used so far, leaving a sizable amount of unspent funding in theory.
Stocker bluntly said Ukraine must transparently explain the source of the new fiscal gap, and he expressed surprise at the figure.

Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico also said after the EU summit that Zelensky is asking the EU for an additional €70 billion loan for 2027, but he has made it clear in negotiations that Slovakia will not take part in that new loan.
Fico argues that Ukraine may ultimately be unable to repay such loans, so the so‑called loan could in practice amount to a grant.

The Czech Republic shares a cautious stance on expanding EU financing for Ukraine. Prime Minister Andrej Babiš opposes inserting the proposed roughly €100 billion Ukraine loan into the next multi‑year EU budget and stresses that the Czech Republic will not provide guarantees for the borrowing.

A European diplomatic source previously disclosed that the International Monetary Fund is expected to publish a new assessment report in November, after which the EU will be able to more accurately gauge Ukraine’s funding needs and discuss whether to issue another joint debt, tap existing budget resources, or ask member states to contribute individually.

Even countries that support aid to Ukraine acknowledge the €70 billion financing challenge. Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal said the EU may need to grant another loan to Ukraine to fill the 2027 fiscal gap.

He believes financial assistance is vital for Ukraine to maintain its war‑fighting capability, but the most likely solution now is another joint EU borrowing. He hopes European nations can finalize the extra 2027 aid by the end of 2026 to avoid being affected by the many national elections slated for next year.
In this context, Marine Le Pen, the far‑right frontrunner for France’s 2027 presidential election, told the media earlier this week that France can no longer shoulder additional Ukraine aid costs.
Le Pen said: "The fair thing to do is to tell Zelensky that, in effect, we are warning him: we cannot provide any more assistance."
She added that if she becomes French president in 2027, she might not support further expansion of Ukraine loans through EU mechanisms.

Regarding the use of frozen Russian assets, Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever stressed on Thursday that the seized assets should be dealt with in a peace settlement after the war, not used now. Frozen Russian assets within the EU exceed €200 billion, the vast majority of which are held by the European Clearing House in Belgium.
Compared with the 2027 funding needs, Ukraine’s demand for air‑defence missiles appears even more urgent.

According to Thursday’s reporting, a source familiar with the situation said Ukraine has exhausted its stock of U.S.‑made Patriot interceptor missiles, leaving it more vulnerable to Russian ballistic missile attacks.
The source noted that in the latest wave of attacks, because of the lack of interceptors, almost all Russian ballistic missiles went uncaught.

But obtaining more interceptors from European countries is equally difficult. European stockpiles are not abundant, global ammunition supplies are tight, and replenishing inventories is under pressure. At the same time, Ukraine’s relationship with the United States remains strained, creating uncertainty about whether European states will be able to secure additional missiles from the U.S.

Media citing a European diplomatic source reported that the Spanish government worries that, because of tense relations between U.S. President Donald Trump and Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, Spain may not be able to obtain sufficient replacement missiles from the United States in the future, prompting a cautious approach to further depleting existing stock.

Greece’s concerns stem mainly from its own security environment. Athens has long feared heightened tensions with neighbouring Turkey and worries that cutting back air‑defence reserves could be perceived as a sign of weakening its own defensive capability.

According to reports, the Trump administration recently warned Ukraine and European allies that if Kyiv does not halt deep strikes on Russian energy facilities, the United States may suspend the arrangement that allows European countries to purchase U.S. weapons for Ukraine.

items.title: 費半連跌八日 黃仁勳：動盪終將過去 AI變革才剛開始
items.title_en: Philadelphia Semiconductor Index Falls Eight Days Straight; Jensen Huang: Turbulence Will Eventually Pass, AI Revolution Only Just Beginning
paras: AI基礎設施熱潮遭遇投資人信心考驗之際，輝達(NVDA-US)執行長黃仁勳公開為AI前景背書，呼籲市場聚焦長期基本面。
黃仁勳週四在柏林接受《彭博社》採訪時表示，眼前的市場動盪「終將過去」，因為AI技術具變革性，將對每個產業和每個國家產生正面影響。他強調，這項進程仍處於起步階段，不會因短期波動而改變。
他表示，「有些消息確實很嘈雜，新聞每天都在發生，但這不會改變基本面。」他也再次強調，「回歸第一性原理，聚焦基本面。」
這番表態發布之際，費城半導體指數已連續第八個交易日下跌，創下2008年以來最長連跌紀錄。輝達股價在過去八個交易日中也有七個交易日收跌。
AI基礎設施企業CoreWeave(CRWV-US)本週同樣承受沉重賣壓，股價單週重挫逾四分之一，公司債券價格也跌至市場通常視為財務困境訊號的水準。輝達是CoreWeave主要股東之一。
目前投資人開始質疑，在借貸成本持續偏高的環境下，AI支出能否維持，以及相關企業能否實現預期獲利。
黃仁勳則預期，企業對AI硬體的大規模投入最終將帶來可觀回報，市場對AI支出可持續性的疑慮，也將隨著技術價值逐步實現而化解。
paras_en: As the AI infrastructure boom faces a test of investor confidence, Nvidia (NVDA-US) CEO Jensen Huang publicly endorsed the AI outlook, urging the market to focus on long‑term fundamentals.

Huang told Bloomberg in an interview in Berlin on Thursday that the current market turbulence “will eventually pass,” because AI technology is transformative and will have a positive impact on every industry and every country. He stressed that the process is still in its early stages and will not be altered by short‑term fluctuations.
He said, “Some news is indeed noisy, and headlines come out every day, but that does not change the fundamentals.” He reiterated, “Return to first‑principles and focus on the fundamentals.”

At the time of his remarks, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had fallen for the eighth consecutive trading day, marking the longest streak since 2008. Nvidia’s stock closed lower on seven of the past eight trading days.

AI infrastructure firm CoreWeave (CRWV-US) also faced heavy selling this week, with its share price plunging more than a quarter over the week and its corporate bonds falling to levels that the market typically interprets as a distress signal. Nvidia is one of CoreWeave’s major shareholders.
Investors are now questioning whether AI spending can be sustained in an environment of persistently high borrowing costs, and whether the related companies can achieve their expected profits.

Huang expects that large‑scale corporate investments in AI hardware will eventually yield substantial returns, and that market concerns about the sustainability of AI spending will dissipate as the technology’s value is gradually realized.

items.title: 知名投資人警告特斯拉多頭 勿炒作與SpaceX合併題材
items.title_en: Prominent Investor Warns Tesla Bulls Against Peddling SpaceX Merger Theme
paras: 《Benzinga》報導，Future Fund管理合夥人Gary Black警告特斯拉(Tesla)(TSLA-US)投資人，不要過度炒作特斯拉可能與馬斯克旗下太空公司SpaceX(SPCX-US)合併的題材。他認為，套利者可能會抵銷任何股東溢價，不過，他也承認新款Roadster跑車雖然對財務的影響有限，卻可能有助於強化品牌。
Black週四在X平台發文表示，「特斯拉多頭應該停止炒作特斯拉與SpaceX的交易。」
他接著指出，「由於這將是一項換股交易，而在這類合併案中，合併後的企業應以估值倍數較低的股票（此處為特斯拉）作為估值基準，因此任何以SpaceX股票支付給特斯拉股東的溢價，都會在交易完成前被套利交易者逐步侵蝕。」
Black的論點假設這筆交易將採取換股方式，且投資人會以估值倍數較低的特斯拉來評價合併後的公司。
他先前曾警告，合併可能使特斯拉估值下降20%至25%，理由包括股東持股遭到稀釋，以及公司可能面臨企業集團折價。
Roadster對獲利貢獻有限 但有助提升品牌價值
Black週五在X平台發文估計，若搭載SpaceX技術的新款Roadster每年交車3,000輛，且每輛車獲利10萬美元，預計2029年將為特斯拉每股盈餘貢獻僅0.06美元。
這相當於市場對特斯拉2029年調整後每股盈餘共識預估值5.40美元的約1.1%。
然而，他認為這款車的飛行能力、加速性能與操控表現，可能為特斯拉整體產品與品牌帶來更大的「光環效應」。
Black仍維持審慎展望，理由包括特斯拉2026年本益比高達230倍、分析師持續下修公司至2030年的獲利預估，以及自動駕駛領域的競爭日益激烈。
Munster與巴克萊看好合併潛力
巴克萊分析師Dan Levy近期表示，特斯拉可能在12月股東大會前宣布合併消息，理由是兩家公司在AI與製造領域具整合機會。
投資人Ross Gerber認為，在Roadster亮相後，SpaceX收購特斯拉「已經顯而易見」，儘管他認為Roadster的推進器技術「只是做做樣子」。
Deepwater Asset Management的Gene Munster同樣將這場展示解讀為馬斯克有意推動合併的跡象。
Munster寫道，「這是一場展現工程實力的表演，除了讓傳統汽車製造商難堪之外，沒有任何商業價值。」他並補充，「Elon已迫不及待要讓特斯拉與SpaceX合而為一。」
paras_en: Benzinga reports that Gary Black, a managing partner at Future Fund, warned Tesla (TSLA-US) investors not to overhype the prospect of a merger with Elon Musk’s space company SpaceX (SPCX-US). He believes arbitrageurs could wipe out any shareholder premium, though he concedes the new Roadster, while having limited financial impact, could help strengthen the brand.
Black posted on X on Thursday that “Tesla bulls should stop hyping a Tesla‑SpaceX deal.”

He added that because the deal would be a stock‑swap transaction, the post‑merger company would be valued using the lower‑multiple stock – in this case Tesla – as the benchmark, so any premium paid in SpaceX shares to Tesla shareholders would be gradually eroded by arbitrage before the deal closes.
Black’s argument assumes the transaction would be executed as a stock swap and that investors would value the combined entity using Tesla’s lower valuation multiple.
He previously warned that the merger could cut Tesla’s valuation by 20%‑25% due to shareholder dilution and a possible conglomerate discount on the combined firm.
Roadster contributes little to earnings but boosts brand value

Black estimated on X on Friday that if the new SpaceX‑technology‑enabled Roadster delivers 3,000 units per year with a $100,000 profit per car, it would add only $0.06 to Tesla’s earnings per share in 2029.
That represents roughly 1.1% of the market’s consensus estimate for Tesla’s adjusted 2029 EPS of $5.40.
However, he believes the car’s flight capability, acceleration and handling could generate a larger “halo effect” for Tesla’s overall product lineup and brand.
Black maintains a cautious outlook, citing Tesla’s projected 2026 P/E of 230×, analysts’ ongoing downward revisions of earnings through 2030, and intensifying competition in autonomous driving.
Munster and Barclays see merger potential
Barclays analyst Dan Levy recently said Tesla could announce a merger before the December shareholders’ meeting, pointing to integration opportunities in AI and manufacturing between the two firms.
Investor Ross Gerber said that after the Roadster debut, a SpaceX acquisition of Tesla “looks obvious,” even though he views the Roadster’s propulsion tech as “just for show.”
Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster likewise read the showcase as a sign that Musk intends to push a merger.
Munster wrote, “It’s a display of engineering prowess that embarrasses traditional automakers but has no commercial value,” adding, “Elon can’t wait to combine Tesla and SpaceX into one.”

items.title: 全球史學界迎「破譯潮」！AI數小時破解200多年前拿破崙寫給法軍將軍密函
items.title_en: Global Historians Welcome a "Decoding Wave"! AI Cracks Napoleon's 200-Year-Old Secret Letter in Hours
paras: 一封沉睡超過200年的拿破崙時期密函，近日被AI在數小時內破譯，對此業內人士稱2026年將成為歷史密碼破譯的轉捩點，AI正深刻改變史學研究的方式。
美國網路安全公司SentinelOne的27歲AI工程師Carter Church，日前靠OpenAI的GPT-6 Astra模型，成功破譯了1809年奉拿破崙之命、由其繼子發給法國將領Auguste de Marmont的加密信件。這封信由24行符號、數字和字母組成，記載了法軍及盟軍的部署位置，該密函之前一直躺在線上學術檔案庫中乏人問津。
Church在9月30日於社交平台發文表示，若不使用數位工具，破譯可能耗時數週，而AI僅用約六小時便完成。他指出，AI最大的優勢在於「不知疲倦」，能持續反覆嘗試。傳統破譯方法雖有效但耗時費力，歷史學家有更重要的問題要解決，許多類似密碼因此長期被擱置。值得一提的是，Church幾乎無需學習破譯技巧或相關歷史知識，便可借助AI完成任務。
完成破譯後，他請日本專利工程師兼歷史密碼網站Cryptiana維護者Satoshi Tomokiyo核驗。Tomokiyo在網站上寫道：「今年將作為歷史密碼破譯的轉捩點被銘記。」
Tomokiyo透露，自9月中以來，清單上的大部分密碼已被AI攻克，使用者既有GPT-6 Astra，也有Anthropic的頂級模型。不過，由於可供AI參考的數據較少，仍有一些難題可能多年無解。AI如此輕易地攻克難題讓他心情複雜，一位同行甚至對他說：「我覺得自己毫無用處。」
事實上，AI對史學研究的影響遠不止破譯密碼。西元79年維蘇威火山爆發時碳化的赫庫蘭尼姆古卷，因過於脆弱無法展開，如今正靠X光掃描和AI分析揭示其中文字。
今年6月，義大利研究人員宣布已利用這一技術首次完整虛擬展開其中一卷，內容是一篇倫理學論著。
AI還被用於轉錄一千萬頁希伯來語手稿，構建可檢索的猶太歷史文化資料庫。相關項目負責人、法國高等研究實踐學院Daniel Stoekl Ben Ezra表示，沒人能處理如此海量的數據，他將這一資料庫比作「過去的超大型Facebook」。
據報道，在巴黎聖母院，一套AI系統已轉錄教堂中世紀檔案中的一萬四千六百頁拉丁文文獻，字符識別率在88%至94%之間，揭示了聖母院日常運作、建築工程及棄兒照料等資訊。
巴黎聖母院檔案研究項目e-NDP負責人、歷史學家Julie Claustre表示，若靠人工完成需要幾十年，但AI不僅僅是節省時間，更讓過去無法開展的研究成為可能。
paras_en: A secret letter from the Napoleonic era that had lain dormant for more than 200 years was recently decoded by AI in just a few hours. Industry insiders say 2026 will become a turning point for breaking historical codes, as AI profoundly reshapes the way historians conduct research.

Carter Church, a 27‑year‑old AI engineer at U.S. cybersecurity firm SentinelOne, used OpenAI’s GPT‑6 Astra model to successfully decode a 1809 encrypted letter sent on Napoleon’s orders by his stepson to French commander Auguste de Marmont. The letter, composed of 24 lines of symbols, numbers and letters, detailed the deployment positions of French and allied forces and had been languishing unnoticed in an online academic archive.

Church posted on social media on September 30 that without digital tools the decoding could have taken weeks, whereas the AI completed it in about six hours. He noted the AI’s biggest advantage is its tirelessness, allowing endless repeated attempts. Traditional decryption methods, while effective, are time‑consuming and labor‑intensive, leaving historians with more pressing questions and many similar codes abandoned. Remarkably, Church needed almost no prior cryptanalysis training or historical knowledge to accomplish the task with AI assistance.

After the decode, he asked Japanese patent engineer and cryptography‑history site maintainer Satoshi Tomokiyo to verify the result. Tomokiyo wrote on the site, “This year will be remembered as a turning point in the decoding of historical ciphers.”

Tomokiyo disclosed that since mid‑September most of the codes on the list have been broken by AI, using both GPT‑6 Astra and Anthropic’s top‑tier models. However, because reference data for AI is limited, some challenges may remain unsolved for years. The ease with which AI cracks these puzzles left him conflicted, and a colleague told him, “I feel completely useless.”

In fact, AI’s impact on historical research goes far beyond codebreaking. The carbonized Herculaneum scrolls, charred by the 79 AD eruption of Vesuvius and too fragile to unroll, are now being revealed through X‑ray scanning and AI analysis of the embedded text.
In June this year, Italian researchers announced they had used this technology to virtually unroll one scroll for the first time, uncovering an ethical treatise within its pages.

AI is also being employed to transcribe ten million pages of Hebrew manuscripts, building a searchable database of Jewish historical and cultural material. Project lead Daniel Stoekl Ben Ezra of France’s École des Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales said no one could handle such a massive dataset, likening the database to “a super‑large Facebook of the past.”

According to reports, an AI system at Notre‑Dame de Paris has transcribed 14,600 pages of medieval Latin documents from the cathedral’s archives, achieving character‑recognition rates between 88% and 94% and revealing details about daily operations, construction projects, and orphan care at the cathedral.

Julie Claustre, head of the e‑NDP Notre‑Dame archive project and a historian, said that doing the work manually would take decades, but AI not only saves time—it makes research that was previously impossible now feasible.

items.title: 新加坡船舶遭攻擊仍不退場！荷姆茲海峽航運業者為何甘冒風險？
items.title_en: Singapore Vessels Attacked Yet Still Sailing: Why Do Houthi Strait Operators Risk It?
paras: 儘管一艘新加坡籍貨櫃船本周遭擊沉，海事專家表示，在中東能源需求強勁、航運商機豐厚的支撐下，商船仍可能持續航行於危險的荷姆茲海峽，部分業者願意冒著日益升高的攻擊風險通行。
最新針對兩艘新加坡籍貨櫃船的攻擊，加深外界對商船在荷姆茲海峽航行安全疑慮。但分析人士指出，即使大型貨櫃航運公司大多仍避開該海峽，相關事件也不太可能讓剩餘航運活動全面停擺。
新加坡南洋理工大學拉惹勒南國際研究院(S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies)資深研究員Collin Koh表示，儘管安全威脅升高，航運公司仍可能繼續尋找通行荷姆茲海峽的機會。
Koh說：「我不認為短期內，新加坡籍船舶或新加坡航運公司必然會在有機會通行時選擇避開。」
本周兩艘在新加坡註冊的貨櫃船GFS Pride與GFS Giselle遭到攻擊，前者遭不明飛行物擊中後起火，最終沉沒，後者則受損。不過兩艘船的船員據報均平安。
海事數據分析公司Kpler指出，在10月14日為止一周，通過荷姆茲海峽的船舶數量降至131艘，低於前一周的176艘，但這項降幅不能完全歸咎於近期攻擊事件。
Kpler海事風險與合規經理Dimitris Ampatzidis表示，這些攻擊凸顯伊朗仍有能力威脅商船，風險影響範圍也不限於石油與天然氣運輸。

商業誘因仍在 高油價支撐航行意願

Koh表示，自衝突爆發以來，全球航運公司一直在尋找通行荷姆茲海峽的機會，部分業者願意承擔更高風險與成本。而亞洲強勁的石油需求，持續為油輪業者提供將能源供應從波斯灣運出的誘因，即使有人身安全威脅和航程更加複雜的挑戰。
Koh指出，即使必須支付額外成本，部分業者仍可能願意冒險一試。
新加坡外交部長Vivian Balakrishnan舉例說明，油價上漲可能讓船舶即使冒著危險通過荷姆茲海峽，仍具商業上的獲利空間。
他談到與一名未具名波灣國家官員的對話，該官員表示，透過一項俗稱「荷姆茲接駁」的運輸模式，讓約20艘超大型原油運輸船往返航行，該國石油出口收入反而高於戰前。
根據這名官員的說法，這些船舶自行承擔遭攻擊的風險，即使較高的原油價格讓航程充滿危險，仍具有財務上的吸引力。
Balakrishnan引述該官員的話說：「有時候會遭到攻擊，但繼續經營『荷姆茲接駁』仍然值得。」
Ampatzidis表示，儘管風險升高，船舶仍持續通過荷姆茲海峽，反映此地的商業重要性，尤其是對供應亞洲市場的能源運輸而言。
不過他也指出，若攻擊事件進一步增加，可能讓更多業者打消通行念頭，實際影響則將因船舶類型及各公司對風險的評估而有所不同。
新加坡航運公會也淡化商業航運全面撤出該區域的可能性，認為業者更可能因應貿易環境變化調整營運模式。公會會長TS Teo表示：「這些發展與其說代表業者全面撤離該區域，不如說更可能促使航運模式調整，以因應商品與能源供需變化。」
他補充，船東在制定營運決策時，仍會持續權衡商業考量、安全情勢與船員安全。

全球貨櫃航運已調整航線 阿曼灣升級衝突恐衝擊供應鏈

儘管部分業者仍願意通行荷姆茲海峽，全球貨櫃航運業多數公司早已調整航線網絡，以避開這條海峽。
Drewry Maritime Advisors董事Jayendu Krishna表示，自2月戰爭爆發、航運公司暫停相關業務以來，主要貨櫃航運公司都尚未恢復經由荷姆茲海峽的服務。只有部分區域業者仍零星提供航運服務，且通常使用規模較小的支線船。
他剖析，這代表近期攻擊對貨櫃航運的直接影響可能有限。
然而，若衝突進一步升級至阿曼灣，區域供應鏈可能面臨更嚴重威脅，尤其是當替代港口受到干擾時。
目前阿拉伯聯合大公國的霍爾法坎港(Khorfakkan)及阿曼的蘇哈爾港(Sohar)，已成為貨物進入波灣國家的重要門戶。Krishna說：「如果阿曼灣成為實際軍事衝突區域，波灣國家的很大一部分物資供應將被切斷，因為霍爾法坎港與蘇哈爾港一直是這些國家的生命線。」
paras_en: Despite a Singapore-flagged container ship being sunk this week, maritime experts say that strong Middle East energy demand and lucrative shipping opportunities could keep merchant vessels navigating the risky Houthi Strait, with some operators willing to face rising attack risks.

The recent attacks on two Singapore-flagged container ships have heightened concerns about safety in the Houthi Strait. However, analysts note that even though most large container carriers avoid the strait, these incidents are unlikely to halt all remaining shipping activity.

Collin Koh, senior researcher at Singapore’s S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies, said that despite heightened security threats, shipping companies may continue to seek opportunities to transit the Houthi Strait.
Koh said, "I don’t think Singapore-flagged vessels or Singaporean shipping companies will necessarily avoid the strait when there is an opportunity to transit in the short term."

This week, two Singapore-registered container ships, GFS Pride and GFS Giselle, were attacked; the former was hit by an unidentified flying object, caught fire and eventually sank, while the latter was damaged. Crew members on both vessels were reported safe.

Maritime data firm Kpler noted that in the week ending October 14, the number of ships passing through the Houthi Strait fell to 131, down from 176 the previous week, but this decline cannot be fully attributed to the recent attacks.
Kpler’s maritime risk and compliance manager Dimitris Ampatzidis said the attacks underscore Iran’s continued ability to threaten merchant vessels, and the risk extends beyond oil and gas transport.

Commercial incentives remain strong, with high oil prices supporting the willingness to sail. Koh said that since the conflict began, global shippers have been looking for ways to use the Houthi Strait, and some operators are prepared to bear higher risks and costs, while robust Asian oil demand continues to motivate tanker operators to move energy from the Persian Gulf despite personal safety threats and more complex voyages.
Koh added that even if it means paying extra costs, some operators may still be willing to take the gamble.
Singapore Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan gave an example, noting that rising oil prices can make it commercially viable for ships to risk transiting the Houthi Strait.

He recounted a conversation with an unnamed Gulf‑state official who said that through a so‑called “Houthi shuttle” transport model, about 20 ultra‑large crude carriers make round‑trip voyages, and the country’s oil export revenue actually exceeds pre‑war levels.
According to that official, the vessels assume the attack risk themselves, and even though higher crude prices make the route hazardous, it remains financially attractive.
Balakrishnan quoted the official: "Sometimes you get attacked, but continuing the ‘Houthi shuttle’ is still worth it."
Ampatzidis said that despite rising risks, ships continue to use the Houthi Strait, reflecting its commercial importance, especially for energy shipments to Asian markets.
He warned, however, that if attacks increase further, more operators might be deterred, with the actual impact varying by vessel type and each company’s risk assessment.

The Singapore Shipping Association downplayed the likelihood of a wholesale withdrawal of commercial shipping from the area, suggesting operators are more likely to adjust their business models in response to changing trade conditions. Association president TS Teo said, "These developments are less about a full exit from the region and more about prompting adjustments in shipping models to match shifts in commodity and energy supply‑demand."
He added that shipowners will continue to weigh commercial considerations, safety conditions, and crew welfare when making operational decisions.
Global container shipping has already rerouted routes, with many carriers upgrading alternatives to avoid the strait amid the conflict’s impact on supply chains.

Drewry Maritime Advisors director Jayendu Krishna noted that since the war began in February and carriers suspended related services, major container lines have not resumed Houthi Strait services. Only some regional players still offer sporadic service, typically with smaller feeder vessels.
He explained that this suggests the direct impact of recent attacks on container shipping may be limited.
However, if the conflict escalates into the Oman Sea, regional supply chains could face far greater threats, especially if alternative ports are disrupted.

Currently, the UAE’s Khorfakkan port and Oman’s Sohar port have become key gateways for goods entering Gulf states. Krishna said, "If the Oman Sea becomes an actual combat zone, a large portion of Gulf‑state supplies will be cut off, because Khorfakkan and Sohar have long been lifelines for those countries."

items.title: 費半創18年最長連跌！黃仁勳釋定心丸：AI市場波動「一切都會過去」
items.title_en: Philadelphia Semiconductor Index Posts Longest Losing Streak in 18 Years; Jensen Huang Offers Reassurance: AI Market Volatility “Will All Pass”
paras: 輝達(NVDA-US)執行長黃仁勳對近期人工智慧(AI)類股遭遇的拋售潮抱持樂觀看法，認為AI技術帶來的效益很快就會超越投資人的疑慮。
黃仁勳周五(16日)在柏林出席一場活動時接受《彭博》訪問，他表示：「這一切都會過去，原因很簡單。這項技術將帶來變革，對每個產業、每個國家都會產生非常正面的影響。毫無疑問，這股趨勢將持續下去，而我們才剛起步。」

晶片股連跌八天 市場憂AI支出難以持續

晶片製造商與AI基礎設施公司股價才剛結束動盪的一周，費城半導體指數連續八個交易日下跌，創2008年以來最長連跌紀錄，輝達股價在過去八個交易日中有七天下跌。
投資人擔憂，不斷攀升的借貸成本可能讓AI支出無以為繼。但黃仁勳始終對AI市場及其對整體經濟的影響抱持樂觀看法，他預期，大規模硬體投資最終將帶來回報，緩解市場的不安情緒。
黃仁勳說：「有些新聞確實會帶來波動。你也知道，新聞隨時都會出現，但這些消息不會改變基本面。」
輝達在全球AI基礎設施建置浪潮中居於核心地位，是AI加速器的最大供應商，這類晶片用於開發及運行AI模型。不僅如此，輝達的業務也已延伸至各類相關硬體、軟體與服務。

CoreWeave債券暴跌 黃仁勳籲聚焦基本面

近期AI類股賣壓對輝達支持的雲端運算服務商CoreWeave(CRWV-US)的衝擊尤其顯著，該公司債券日前跌到通常反映財務壓力的價位，本周股價也下跌四分之一。
輝達不僅是CoreWeave的重要供應商，也是其第二大股東，持股約10%，讓兩家公司的關係格外受到關注。
面對市場波動，黃仁勳一再呼籲投資人不要只關注短期消息，應該著眼於這項技術的長期價值。他說：「要專注於第一性原理，也就是最根本的原則。要專注於基本面。」
(本文不開放合作夥伴轉載)
paras_en: Nvidia (NVDA-US) CEO Jensen Huang remains optimistic about the recent sell‑off in AI‑related stocks, believing the benefits of AI technology will quickly outweigh investors' concerns.

Huang told Bloomberg during an event in Berlin on Friday the 16th, "It will all pass, and the reason is simple. This technology will be transformative and will have a very positive impact on every industry and every country. There’s no doubt this trend will continue, and we’re only just getting started."

Chip stocks have fallen for eight consecutive days, raising worries that AI spending may not be sustainable. After a week of turbulence, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index has logged eight straight session losses, the longest streak since 2008, and Nvidia’s share price has declined on seven of those eight days.

Investors fear that rising borrowing costs could choke AI expenditures. Nevertheless, Huang stays bullish on the AI market and its broader economic impact, expecting large‑scale hardware investments to eventually pay off and ease market anxiety.
Huang said, "Some news does cause volatility. You know news comes out all the time, but those headlines don’t change the fundamentals."

Nvidia sits at the core of the global AI infrastructure build‑out, being the largest supplier of AI accelerators—chips used to develop and run AI models. Moreover, Nvidia’s business now spans a wide range of related hardware, software, and services.

CoreWeave bonds have plunged, and Huang urged focus on fundamentals. The recent AI‑stock sell‑pressure has hit cloud‑computing provider CoreWeave (CRWV-US), which Huang backs, hard; its bonds fell to levels that typically signal financial stress, and its stock dropped a quarter this week.
Nvidia is not only a key supplier to CoreWeave but also its second‑largest shareholder, owning about 10%, drawing extra attention to the relationship between the two companies.

Amid market swings, Huang repeatedly tells investors not to fixate on short‑term headlines but to look at the long‑term value of the technology. He said, "Focus on first‑principles, the most fundamental rules. Focus on the fundamentals."

本週公布的消費者物價與生產者物價數據均高於預期，一度令市場感到不安。不過，聯準會官員的談話顯示，目前沒有急於進一步緊縮貨幣政策的必要，有助於穩定美國公債殖利率，也削弱了美元的支撐力道。
AI類股本週大幅下跌，壓力也蔓延至部分信用市場。由於投資人已大量押注AI供應鏈各個環節，如今開始擔心資料中心營運商可能無法及時實現獲利，進而償還債務。
StoneX全球市場研究主管Matt Weller表示，「我認為今天乃至本週最值得關注的現象，是美元與AI交易之間的緊密連動。通常科技股遭到拋售時，市場會預期美元因避險需求而走強。我們確實看到部分資金流向債券，但美元實際上卻在下跌。」
本週英鎊與瑞士法郎兌美元的升幅居前。瑞士法郎受到避險需求支撐，市場也預期，即使利率環境進一步走低，瑞士仍不太可能將政策利率降至目前零利率以下。

紐約梅隆銀行宏觀經濟策略師John Velis表示，「我認為，目前聯準會決策委員會內部，尤其是理事們，尚未形成足夠共識支持10月升息。不過，12月是否升息仍是未解之題，從現在到那時還有許多事情可能發生。」

法國財政風險仍是市場關注的背景因素。10月初，法國債務風險溢價曾大幅攀升。

投資人預期，美國總統川普將避免讓中東或烏克蘭局勢進一步升級，因為更大規模的衝突可能推升通膨，進而損害他在期中選舉前的政治支持度。

paras_en: The dollar fell on Friday (the 16th), with both the euro and the yen posting their first weekly depreciation in more than a month, reflecting a cooling of market expectations for further Fed rate hikes and lingering investor worries that AI is weighing on equity markets.
In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, slipped 0.17% to 101.87, down about 0.35% for the week.

Consumer price and producer price data released this week came in above expectations, briefly unsettling markets. However, comments from Fed officials indicated no urgent need for further monetary tightening, helping to stabilise US Treasury yields and weakening support for the dollar.

AI‑related stocks fell sharply this week, and the pressure spread to parts of the credit market. Investors, who have heavily bet on every link of the AI supply chain, are now worried that data‑center operators may not generate profits quickly enough to service their debt.

Matt Weller, head of global market research at StoneX, said, "I think the most noteworthy phenomenon today and this week is the tight link between the dollar and AI trading. Usually when tech stocks are sold off, the market expects the dollar to strengthen on safe‑haven demand. We did see some flows into bonds, but the dollar actually fell."

The pound and the Swiss franc posted the biggest gains against the dollar this week. The franc was supported by safe‑haven demand, and markets expect that even if rates fall further, Switzerland is unlikely to push its policy rate below the current zero‑percent level.
The pound rose 0.31% to $1.3314, up 0.63% for the week.
The dollar slipped 0.25% against the Swiss franc to 0.8246 CHF, down 0.67% for the week. The franc had appreciated more than 1.4% over the past two trading days.
CME’s FedWatch tool shows the market now assigns an 83% probability that the Fed will keep rates unchanged later this month, up from 49% a month ago.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh attended the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Friday and offered no clues about future rate decisions, saying he does not "pre‑judge" the outcome of any meeting.

John Velis, macro strategy strategist at BNY Mellon, said, "I think the Fed’s policy committee, especially the governors, have not yet reached sufficient consensus to support a rate hike in October. However, whether there will be a hike in December remains an open question, and many things could happen between now and then."
Euro‑area fiscal risks remain a focus.
Fiscal risk in France continues to be a background concern for markets, with French sovereign risk premiums spiking sharply in early October.
The euro rose 0.08% to $1.1227. It had gained 0.56% on Thursday, the biggest single‑day rise in two months, and is up about 0.23% for the week.

Investors expect that President Trump will try to avoid further escalation in the Middle East or Ukraine, as a larger conflict could push inflation higher and damage his political support ahead of the mid‑term elections.
The dollar fell 0.08% to ¥158.11, ending a four‑week streak of depreciation for the yen, which rose 0.13% this week. Previously, the Iran conflict had supported a stronger dollar.
Recent oil price gains have lifted the dollar while putting pressure on currencies of energy‑importing countries such as the euro and yen.
Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda reiterated on Friday that a potential inflation rate above the BOJ’s 2% target remains a risk to watch.

items.title_en: Taiwan Dollar Weakens While Stocks Hold, Falling 0.73 ¢ to Slip Below the 32.3 TWD Mark
paras: 在美元指數維持強勢、外資持續撤出亞洲市場影響下，新台幣兌美元今 (16) 日走弱，終場收在32.338元，貶值7.3分，續創近期波段低點，顯示國際資金仍偏向美元資產，相較於昨天的91億美元爆巨量，台北外匯經紀公司與元太外匯經紀公司合計總成交量為 46.12億美元。
儘管匯市承壓，台股表現相對有撐，加權指數終場收在47,111點，上漲141點，漲幅約0.3%，呈現匯弱股強格局。市場買盤主要聚焦 AI 伺服器、高階 PCB 及半導體供應鏈族群，在電子權值股支撐下，大盤成功守住漲勢。
從籌碼面來看，統計今日三大法人合計賣超約729億元，其中外資賣超高達494億元，已連續第8個交易日站在賣方；投信則持續扮演護盤角色，買超約132億元，寫下連6買；自營商賣超約367億元。
市場人士指出，本波新台幣轉弱主要受到美元升值效應帶動，近期美國經濟數據維持韌性，加上市場重新評估聯準會後續政策路徑，推升美元買盤，亞洲主要貨幣同步承壓，新台幣也不例外。資料顯示，10月以來新台幣已由31字頭一路走貶至32.3元以上水準。
觀察資金流向，外資近期持續調節台股權值股與電子類股部位，成為匯市與股市的重要變數。不過投信買盤明顯進場承接，加上AI相關產業基本面未見轉弱，因此支撐台股維持高檔震盪格局。今天市場呈現「匯率偏空、股市偏多」，除外資匯出導致台幣走弱，加上AI、高效能運算(HPC)及先進封裝需求仍強，吸引國內資金與長線買盤進駐，使台股維持相對強勢。
paras_en: Under a strong US dollar index and continued foreign‑capital outflows from Asian markets, the New Taiwan dollar weakened against the US dollar today (Oct 16), closing at 32.338 TWD, down 0.73 ¢ and extending its recent low‑point swing, indicating that international funds remain biased toward dollar assets. In contrast to yesterday’s massive USD 91 billion turnover, Taipei’s foreign‑exchange brokers and Yuan‑Tai FX brokers together handled a total volume of USD 46.12 billion.

Despite pressure on the currency market, Taiwan’s equity market showed relative resilience, with the weighted index closing at 47,111 points, up 141 points or about 0.3%, reflecting a “weak currency, strong stocks” pattern. Buying interest centered on AI servers, high‑end PCBs and semiconductor supply‑chain groups, and the rally in heavyweight electronics stocks helped the market maintain its upward momentum.

From a flow perspective, the three major institutional investors sold a combined net NT$729 billion today, with foreign investors leading the sell‑side at NT$494 billion for the eighth consecutive trading day. Trust funds continued to play a stabilising role, net‑buying about NT$132 billion for the sixth straight session, while proprietary traders sold roughly NT$367 billion.

Market observers said the recent weakening of the Taiwan dollar is mainly driven by the dollar’s appreciation. Recent US economic data remain resilient and the market’s reassessment of the Fed’s policy path has boosted dollar demand, putting pressure on major Asian currencies, including the TWD. Data show that since October the Taiwan dollar has slid from the low‑31s to above the 32.3 TWD level.

Looking at capital flows, foreign investors have been adjusting their positions in Taiwan’s heavyweight and electronics stocks, becoming a key variable for both the FX and equity markets. However, trust‑fund buying is evident, and the fundamentals of AI‑related industries have not weakened, supporting the Taiwan stock market’s high‑level range‑bound pattern. Today’s market displayed a “bearish currency, bullish equity” stance: foreign outflows weakened the TWD, while strong demand for AI, high‑performance computing and advanced packaging kept domestic and long‑term buying interest in equities, allowing the stock market to stay relatively strong.

paras: 美元周四(15日)自18個月高點回落，投資人將目光從強勁的美國通膨與消費支出數據，轉向 AI 資料中心業者債券遭拋售的情況。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)下跌 0.45%，報 101.99。此前美國通膨數據高於預期，美元指數週三升至 18 個月高點。
美國 9 月生產者物價(PPI)以 4 年半來最快速度上漲，商品與服務成本同步增加，進一步顯示通膨壓力正從能源領域擴散至其他領域。
上個月零售銷售增幅高於預期，主要受到汽油價格上漲帶動，每週初領失業救濟金人數則小幅增加，顯示消費需求仍具韌性，勞動市場也維持穩定。
但美國公債價格上漲，美元則回落，反映聯準會(Fed)官員近期發表審慎言論，進一步降低市場對 10 月升息的預期。
Monex USA交易主管 Juan Perez 表示，「目前市場存在一種不利美元的論述，原因在於，通膨若維持在這樣的水準，且以如此快的速度上升，將難以持續。」
他表示，「無論戰事方面沒有好消息，或股市前景看起來悲觀，在過去四週美元大幅走強之後，市場仍傾向拋售美元……經濟停滯似乎對交易員的想法產生更大的影響。」
AI企業債務負擔受關注
美元回落帶動歐元反彈，歐元兌美元上漲 0.56%，從 18 個月低點升至 1.1218 美元，創下近兩個月來最大單日漲幅。
英鎊兌美元則上漲 0.64%，至 1.3275 美元，此前數據顯示，英國經濟 8 月意外成長 0.1%。
週三美國消費者物價指數（CPI）數據高於預期，最初推升市場對聯準會維持高利率更長時間的押注。同時，市場再度擔憂 AI 企業沉重的債務負擔，促使資金流向美國公債等避險資產，市場走勢因而震盪加劇。
Mesirow Currency Management 資深投資策略師 Uto Shinohara 表示，「晶片股遭拋售為債券提供支撐，使殖利率得以維持在相對受控的水準，抵銷通膨訊號帶來的影響。」
芝商所（CME Group）FedWatch 工具顯示，交易員目前預期，聯準會在 10 月 27 日至 28 日的會議上維持利率不變的機率為 73%，高於一個月前的 53%。
CPI 報告公布後，市場對升息的預期機率大幅上升，但聯準會負責監管事務的副主席鮑曼 (Michelle Bowman)，以及舊金山聯準銀行總裁戴莉 (Mary Daly) 等官員表示，聯準會可以等到會議前取得更明確的資訊再做決定，隨後市場對升息的押注便有所降溫。
LMAX Group 市場策略師 Joel Kruger 表示，「如果殖利率難以進一步走高，而美元每逢反彈便持續遭到賣出，將會強化我們的看法：通膨消息大致已被市場消化，風險的整體平衡將有利於風險性資產。」
投資人週五也將關注聯準會官員在曼谷舉行的國際貨幣基金（IMF）與世界銀行年度會議上的談話，包括聯準會主席華許 (Kevin Warsh)，以尋找美國央行下一步行動的線索。
澳幣兌美元下跌 0.77%，至 0.6919 美元，此前澳洲 9 月就業人數意外減少。
日元則升值 0.15%，至每美元兌 158.08 日元。
Shinohara 表示，「聯準會即將進入政策會議前的靜默期，而會議前也不再有一級重要經濟數據公布，因此市場走勢可能仍將受到俄羅斯與烏克蘭、伊朗相關地緣政治不確定性，以及 AI 產業發展的影響。」

paras_en: The dollar fell on Thursday (the 15th) from an 18‑month high as investors shifted their focus from strong U.S. inflation and consumer spending data to the sell‑off in bonds of AI data‑center operators.

In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, slipped 0.45% to 101.99. Earlier, U.S. inflation data came in above expectations, pushing the index to an 18‑month peak on Wednesday.

U.S. September producer prices (PPI) rose at the fastest pace in four and a half years, with costs for goods and services climbing together, further showing inflation pressure spreading from the energy sector to other areas.

Last month’s retail sales growth exceeded expectations, driven mainly by higher gasoline prices, while initial unemployment claims rose slightly, indicating consumer demand remains resilient and the labor market stays stable.
However, U.S. Treasury prices rose and the dollar retreated, reflecting recent cautious remarks from Federal Reserve officials that further lowered market expectations of a rate hike in October.

Juan Perez, head of trading at Monex USA, said, "There is currently a narrative that is unfavorable to the dollar because if inflation stays at this level and rises this quickly, it will be hard to sustain."

He added, "Whether there is no good news on the war front or the equity outlook looks bleak, after the dollar’s strong run over the past four weeks the market still tends to sell the greenback… stagnation seems to have a bigger impact on traders’ thinking."
AI companies' debt burdens draw attention
The dollar’s decline lifted the euro, which rose 0.56% against the dollar from an 18‑month low to $1.1218, marking the biggest single‑day gain in nearly two months.
The pound rose 0.64% to $1.3275 after data showed the U.K. economy unexpectedly grew 0.1% in August.

Wednesday’s U.S. consumer price index (CPI) came in above expectations, initially boosting bets that the Fed would keep rates high for longer. At the same time, renewed worries about heavy debt loads at AI firms prompted a flow into safe‑haven assets such as U.S. Treasuries, intensifying market volatility.

Uto Shinohara, senior investment strategist at Mesirow Currency Management, said, "The sell‑off in chip stocks provided support for bonds, keeping yields at relatively controlled levels and offsetting the impact of inflation signals."
The CME Group FedWatch tool shows traders now assign a 73% probability that the Fed will leave rates unchanged at its Oct. 27‑28 meeting, up from 53% a month ago.

After the CPI report, the market’s probability of a rate hike surged, but Fed Vice‑Chair Michelle Bowman and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said the Fed could wait for clearer information before deciding, cooling the market’s rate‑hike bets.

LMAX Group market strategist Joel Kruger said, "If yields struggle to rise further and the dollar keeps getting sold each time it rebounds, it reinforces our view that inflation news has largely been priced in and the overall risk balance will favor risky assets."
Investors will also watch Friday for comments from Fed officials at the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, including Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, for clues on the central bank’s next move.
The Australian dollar fell 0.77% to $0.6919 after September job numbers in Australia unexpectedly dropped.
The yen appreciated 0.15% to 158.08 per dollar.

Shinohara noted, "The Fed is entering a pre‑meeting quiet period, and no major economic data will be released before the meeting, so market moves may still be influenced by geopolitical uncertainties related to Russia, Ukraine, Iran, and the development of the AI industry."

items.title: 〈台幣〉股匯雙殺再現！匯市爆91億美元巨量 重摔近2角收32.265元
items.title_en: Taiwan Dollar Faces Dual Stock‑Currency Slump Again! FX Market Swells to $9.115 Billion, Drops Nearly 2 ¢ to 32.265
paras: 台北外匯市場今(15)日上演股匯雙殺戲碼，在外資大舉撤出、台股重挫逾千點衝擊下，新台幣兌美元匯率終場收在32.265元，重貶1.92角，成交金額更放大至 91.15 億美元，顯示市場避險情緒急遽升溫。今日外資及陸資單日淨賣超逾3000億元，成新台幣重貶的最大主因。
新台幣今日以32.11元開出後一路走弱，盤中最低來到32.452元，最低一度崩跌 3.79 角，終場收32.265元，改寫逾 2 個月新低。台北及元太外匯市場總成交量爆出 91.15 億美元的天量，直接打破歷史單日最高成交量紀錄。
匯銀人士指出，今日新台幣走勢主要受到外資大規模匯出影響，而背後關鍵則來自台股出現恐慌性賣壓。市場憂心全球科技股修正及資金風險偏好下降，導致外資同步在股市與匯市進行調節。
觀察今日台股表現，加權指數終場收在46969.87點，大跌1655.96點，跌幅達3.41%，成交值約新台幣1.43兆元，市場氣氛急速轉弱。
法人動向更顯示資金撤離力道驚人。根據證交所統計，三大法人今日合計賣超3700.76億元，其中外資及陸資賣超3025.55億元，自營商賣超958.24億元，僅投信逆勢買超283.03億元。進一步觀察，外資及陸資今日賣出金額高達6773.6億元，遠高於買進的3748.05億元，單日淨賣超逾3000億元，成為新台幣重貶的重要推手。
市場人士分析，近期美元續獲避險資金青睞，加上美債殖利率維持高檔，使亞洲貨幣普遍承壓。加上台股面臨外資調節電子權值股壓力，連帶新台幣跌勢較區域貨幣更加明顯。且今日匯市成交量明顯放大至逾91億美元，遠高於一般交易日水準，反映出口商、進口商及外資同步進場調節部位。
從技術面觀察，新台幣近期持續在32元整數關卡附近震盪，今日收盤已回落至32.265元，代表市場短線仍以美元需求為主。若後續外資持續匯出，不排除匯價仍有測試32.3元至32.5元區間的可能。
今日股匯市同步大幅震盪，也凸顯國際資金流向已成為牽動台灣金融市場的關鍵因素，後續外資是否止血，將成為觀察新台幣能否穩住32元關卡的重要指標。
paras_en: Taipei’s foreign‑exchange market staged a double‑whammy of stocks and currency today (15th), as foreign investors pulled out en masse and the Taiwan stock index plunged over a thousand points. The New Taiwan dollar closed at 32.265 per US dollar, a depreciation of 1.92 ¢, with transaction volume ballooning to $9.115 billion, indicating a sharp rise in market hedging sentiment. Foreign and mainland Chinese investors posted a net sell‑off of more than NT$300 billion for the day, the main driver of the dollar’s steep fall.

The New Taiwan dollar opened at 32.11 and weakened throughout the session, hitting a low of 32.452, a drop of 3.79 ¢ at its deepest point, and closed at 32.265, breaking a more‑than‑two‑month low. The Taipei and Yuan‑Tai foreign‑exchange markets together recorded a record‑high daily turnover of $9.115 billion, shattering the previous single‑day volume record.

Currency‑bank officials said the dollar’s move was mainly driven by massive foreign‑exchange outflows from overseas investors, with the underlying cause being panic selling in the Taiwan stock market. The market fears a correction in global tech stocks and a decline in risk appetite, prompting foreign investors to adjust positions in both equities and FX simultaneously.

Looking at today’s stock performance, the weighted index closed at 46,969.87 points, down 1,655.96 points or 3.41%, with a turnover of about NT$1.43 trillion, reflecting a rapid weakening of market sentiment.

Institutional flows further highlight the magnitude of capital outflows. According to exchange statistics, the three major institutional groups sold a combined NT$370.076 billion today, with foreign and mainland Chinese investors net‑selling NT$302.555 billion and proprietary traders selling NT$95.824 billion, while only investment trusts bought a net NT$28.303 billion. More specifically, foreign and mainland Chinese investors sold NT$677.36 billion versus purchases of NT$374.805 billion, a net daily sell‑off of over NT$300 billion, becoming a key force behind the dollar’s sharp depreciation.

Market analysts note that the US dollar continues to attract safe‑haven flows, and US Treasury yields remain high, putting pressure on Asian currencies. Coupled with foreign investors trimming exposure to Taiwan’s heavy‑weight electronic stocks, the New Taiwan dollar has weakened more than regional peers. Today’s FX turnover surged past $9.1 billion, far above normal trading‑day levels, reflecting exporters, importers and foreign investors all adjusting positions together.

From a technical perspective, the New Taiwan dollar has been oscillating around the 32.00 mark. Today’s close at 32.265 suggests short‑term market demand remains dollar‑driven. If foreign outflows persist, further testing of the 32.30‑32.50 range cannot be ruled out.

The simultaneous large swings in stocks and FX today underscore that international capital flows have become a pivotal driver of Taiwan’s financial markets. Whether foreign investors can halt the outflow will be a key gauge for the dollar’s ability to hold the 32.00 level going forward.

items.title: 瑞銀維持美元「逢低買進」策略
items.title_en: UBS Maintains "Buy the Dip" Strategy for the Dollar
paras: 《Investing.com》報導，瑞銀(UBS)週三(14日)在給客戶的報告中表示，只要能源價格維持高檔，且AI投資題材持續發酵，逢美元回檔時買進仍是合適的策略。
策略師Shahab Jalinoos表示，G10貨幣市場本週走勢相對平淡，法國與德國10年期公債殖利率利差穩定在約140個基點。
他指出，從法國的角度來看，這個利差水準仍令人不安，也持續支持歐元兌美元應採取「逢高賣出」策略的觀點。
瑞銀預期，歐元將測試第四季的區間低點1.1050，並維持2026年底目標價1.1200不變。
Jalinoos指出，柴油價格可能接近穩定的初步跡象，為歐元提供部分支撐。然而，歐洲仍面臨風險，天然氣庫存處於異常低檔，天然氣期貨價格也升至本輪週期新高。
近期科技股走勢疲軟，可能促使美元進入部分整理階段，通膨數據也可能進一步降低市場對未來較長期間升息的預期。
他寫道，「儘管如此，我們的核心觀點仍未改變：只要能源價格維持高檔，且AI帶動的投資題材持續發酵，逢美元走低時買進仍是合適的策略。」
在商品貨幣方面，瑞銀認為，澳幣、紐幣與加幣目前處於整理階段，但由於市場對升息的定價有限，這三種貨幣都有機會收復9月的跌幅。其中，加幣是瑞銀最偏好的短線做多標的。
Jalinoos也反駁了「日本減持法國債券將推升日元」的看法。他表示，國際收支數據顯示，日本對法國債券的曝險部位已大幅下降。
paras_en: Investing.com reported that UBS on Wednesday (the 14th) said in a client report that as long as energy prices stay high and AI‑related investment themes keep developing, buying the dollar on dips remains an appropriate strategy.
Strategist Shahab Jalinoos noted that G10 currency markets were relatively flat this week, with the spread between French and German 10‑year government bond yields steady at about 140 basis points.
He pointed out that from a French perspective this spread level is still unsettling and continues to support the view that the euro versus the dollar should be sold on rallies.
UBS expects the euro to test the fourth‑quarter low of 1.1050 and keeps its year‑end‑2026 target unchanged at 1.1200.

Jalinoos said diesel prices may be showing early signs of stabilisation, offering some support to the euro. However, Europe still faces risks as natural‑gas inventories are at unusually low levels and gas futures have risen to a new high for this cycle.
Weakness in recent tech stocks could push the dollar into a partial correction, and inflation data may further reduce market expectations for prolonged rate hikes.

He wrote, "Nevertheless, our core view remains unchanged: as long as energy prices stay high and AI‑driven investment themes continue to develop, buying the dollar on its declines remains an appropriate strategy."

Regarding commodity currencies, UBS sees the Australian, New Zealand and Canadian dollars as currently in a consolidation phase, but with limited rate‑hike pricing in the market each has a chance to recover September losses. The Canadian dollar is UBS’s top short‑term long‑biased pick.

Jalinoos also rebutted the view that Japan’s reduction of French bond holdings would boost the yen, noting that balance‑of‑payments data show Japan’s exposure to French bonds has already fallen sharply.

paras: 美元周三(14日)觸及至18個月高點，美國通膨數據強於預期，一度重新點燃市場對聯準會(Fed)可能在本月稍晚升息的預期。不過，隨著投資人重新預期聯準會將保持耐心，美元隨後自高點回落。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)上漲0.34%，報102.53，稍早在上午尾盤一度升至102.94。
美國勞工部勞工統計局公布的數據顯示，由於汽油價格大幅上漲，美國9月消費者物價明顯攀升。
State Street資深全球市場策略師Marvin Loh表示，「CPI數據仍在影響市場估值，而股市下跌又提供了另一個推升美元的理由。」
這份通膨報告蓋過了聯準會官員近期釋出的鴿派訊號，包括紐約聯準銀行總裁威廉斯(John Williams)的言論。他的評論曾在前一個交易日導致美元走弱。
聯準會負責監管事務的副主席鮑曼(Michelle Bowman)週四也釋出訊號，表示在再次升息之前，將採取觀望態度。
另一方面，聯準會週三公布的「褐皮書」顯示，美國勞動市場仍處於「低聘僱、低解僱」狀態，但部分地區的通膨壓力有所升高。
Mesirow Currency Management資深投資策略師Uto Shinohara表示，「聯準會的雙重使命與勞動市場疲弱的跡象之間，仍存在拉鋸。明天公布的零售銷售、初領失業救濟金人數及生產者物價指數(PPI)，應能讓我們更清楚掌握消費者狀況、勞動市場與物價壓力。」
芝商所(CME Group)的FedWatch工具顯示，交易員目前預期聯準會在10月27日至28日的會議上維持利率不變的機率為65%，高於一個月前的53%。市場預期截至2027年底，累計緊縮幅度約為79個基點。
美國央行上個月將政策利率調升0.25個百分點，使利率區間升至3.75%至4.00%。
Angeles Investments投資長Michael Rosen表示，投資人對美國是否願意採取行動抑制通膨，正逐漸失去信心。
Rosen表示，「我們看到……美元走強受到較高利率的支撐。除非聯準會大幅升息、促使經濟陷入衰退，或是我們修正貿易與移民政策，否則通膨不會下降。」
歐元面臨壓力
多國財政與金融主管目前齊聚曼谷，出席國際貨幣基金(IMF)與世界銀行(World Bank)的年度會議。
IMF財政事務主管Rodrigo Valdes表示，IMF已提高對各國政府控制不斷攀升債務的呼籲力度。IMF總裁Kristalina Georgieva則表示，美國需要進行財政調整，讓債務走上更可持續的道路。
法國公債是近期全球債券拋售潮中受衝擊最嚴重市場之一。投資人擔心，明年總統大選前的政治角力，可能阻礙法國降低高額財政赤字的努力。
歐洲央行(ECB)總裁拉加德(Christine Lagarde)在曼谷出席CNN活動時表示，法國應透過財政整頓解決債務問題。這番言論降低了市場對歐洲央行可能開始買進法國公債、以壓低殖利率的猜測。
由於油價上漲，加上市場持續擔憂法國的財政狀況，歐元進一步承壓。
歐元下跌0.41%，至1.1152美元，兌美元匯率創下17個月新低，兌英鎊則跌至16個月新低。
UniCredit外匯策略師Roberto Mialich表示，歐元短期內可能測試1.10美元，但對年底前的歐元走勢，他的看法沒有那麼悲觀。他預期，「美國公債殖利率可能回落，儘管歐元區情勢仍可能對歐元構成壓力。」
《金融時報》週三報導，英國財政大臣John Healey預計，本月預算案中所有新增的支出措施，都將透過加稅或削減支出來支應，而非增加借款。
IMF一名高階官員表示，該機構並未建議英國加快財政整頓的步伐。

paras_en: The dollar hit an 18‑month high on Wednesday (the 14th) as U.S. inflation data came in stronger than expected, briefly reigniting market expectations that the Federal Reserve might raise rates later this month. However, as investors revised their outlook to see the Fed staying patient, the dollar retreated from its peak.
In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, rose 0.34% to 102.53, after having briefly climbed to 102.94 earlier in the session.
Data released by the U.S. Labor Department’s Bureau of Labor Statistics showed that September’s consumer price index rose sharply, driven by a large jump in gasoline prices.
State Street senior global markets strategist Marvin Loh said, “CPI data is still influencing market valuations, and the stock market decline provides another reason to push the dollar higher.”

The inflation report eclipsed recent dovish signals from Fed officials, including comments from New York Fed President John Williams, whose remarks had weakened the dollar on the previous trading day.
Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman also signaled on Thursday that the central bank would adopt a wait‑and‑see stance before any further rate hikes.
Meanwhile, the Fed’s Beige Book released on Wednesday showed that the U.S. labor market remains in a “low‑hiring, low‑layoff” environment, though inflation pressures have risen in some regions.

Mesirow Currency Management senior investment strategist Uto Shinohara said, “The Fed’s dual mandate is still at odds with signs of a weakening labor market. Tomorrow’s retail sales, initial jobless claims and producer price index (PPI) data should give us a clearer picture of consumer conditions, the labor market and price pressures.”

CME Group’s FedWatch tool shows traders now assign a 65% probability that the Fed will keep rates unchanged at its Oct. 27‑28 meeting, up from 53% a month ago. The market expects a cumulative tightening of about 79 basis points by the end of 2027.
The U.S. central bank raised its policy rate by 0.25 percentage point last month, moving the target range to 3.75%‑4.00%.
Angeles Investments chief investment officer Michael Rosen said investors are losing confidence that the United States will take decisive action to curb inflation.

Rosen added, “We see the dollar’s strength being supported by higher rates. Unless the Fed hikes aggressively enough to push the economy into recession, or we overhaul trade and immigration policy, inflation won’t come down.”
Euro Under Pressure
Finance and central‑bank leaders from multiple countries are gathered in Bangkok for the International Monetary Fund and World Bank annual meetings.

IMF finance chief Rodrigo Valdes said the Fund has stepped up its calls for governments to rein in soaring debt. IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva added that the United States needs fiscal adjustments to put its debt on a more sustainable path.

French sovereign bonds have been among the hardest hit in the recent global bond sell‑off. Investors worry that political battles ahead of next year’s presidential election could hamper France’s efforts to reduce its large fiscal deficit.

European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde, speaking at a CNN event in Bangkok, said France should address its debt problem through fiscal consolidation. Her remarks dampened market speculation that the ECB might start buying French bonds to lower yields.
Higher oil prices and continued concerns about France’s fiscal health have added further pressure on the euro.
The euro fell 0.41% to $1.1152, hitting a 17‑month low against the dollar and a 16‑month low against the pound.

UniCredit foreign‑exchange strategist Roberto Mialich said the euro could test $1.10 in the short term, but he is less pessimistic about its trajectory by year‑end, expecting “U.S. Treasury yields may retreat even though euro‑area conditions could still weigh on the euro.”

The Financial Times reported on Wednesday that UK Treasury Secretary John Healey expects all new spending announced in this month’s budget to be funded by tax hikes or cuts rather than additional borrowing.
An IMF senior official said the institution has not advised the United Kingdom to accelerate its fiscal consolidation pace.
The pound slipped 0.59% to $1.3177.
The dollar fell 0.08% against the yen, to ¥158.16.
